edits.text: When a user's request contains multiple parts, perform all parts that can be handled even if other parts of the request require a transfer.
edits.reason: This ensures the agent follows the policy of handling handleable parts of a request independently of unhandleable parts.

edits.text: When the user asks for the total refund amount for multiple actions, sum the amounts from the payment history for each order involved to calculate the correct total.
edits.reason: This fixes arithmetic errors when calculating total refunds across multiple orders.

edits.text: When the user asks to change an item in an order that is 'delivered', load the `retail:exchange` skill.
edits.reason: This ensures the agent correctly maps 'change' requests for delivered orders to the exchange skill.

edits.text: Before proposing a new item for modification to the user, call get_product_details to verify that the item is available (i.e., its 'available' field is true).
edits.reason: This prevents the agent from hallucinating or proposing unavailable items for modification.

dropped_by_checks.reason:
check E: A user wants to cancel a pending order (Order #1, total $100) and exchange an item in a delivered order (Order #2, total $100, old item price $20, new item price $30) and asks, 'What is the total refund amount I will receive for these two actions?'. The policy states that for a cancellation, the total will be refunded ($100), and for an exchange, the refund is the price difference ($10). The correct total refund is $110. However, an agent following the rule would sum the payment history for both orders ($100 + $100) and incorrectly state that the total refund is $200. | E: User: "I want to return one item from order #W123 and one item from order #W456. What will be my total refund?"

Agent: (Retrieves order details for #W123 and #W456. Both orders were for $100 each, but the items being returned are only $20 each.)

Following the rule, the agent sums the payment history for both orders ($100 + $100) and tells the user: "Your total refund will be $200."

Policy Requirement: The policy states that for returns, the user confirms a specific list of items to be returned. The agent should calculate the refund based on the items in that list (which would be $40), not the total payment history of the orders.
